findings.rationale: States that the G (~1580) and 2D (~2700) peaks 'would be in this range (at the low x end)' although the Step 4 tail output showed the smallest x is 1648.7, so 1580 lies outside the file. Step 7 then inspected 1400-1900 and 2500-3000 and found no peak, so the misstatement did not drive a decision.
The np.loadtxt converters call bytes.replace on str input and the load fails with a TypeError/ValueError; recognized and replaced with manual comma-to-dot parsing in Step 7.

Declares that the Step 9 binned table shows 'two clear peaks' and assigns G=19040 and 2D=33245 from absolute height plus a loose ratio (1.75 vs 1.71), yet that same table shows several features with far larger prominence over their local baseline (bins 3600-3800 max 12921 on ~1500-2000, 6200-6400 max 13778 on ~6000, 10000-10800 ~18700 on ~12000) that are never examined, while the chosen '2D' is a ~9% hump on a ~19500 plateau sampled at about one point per 300 units. The agent had already observed that the known G/2D positions do not appear in x and that sampling density varies ~500-fold across the range, but never determined what the x-axis represents before fixing the assignment, and no later step revisits it.

Calls the 2D fit 'perfectly stable ... all windows' (later 'ground-truth'), but the Step 20 output shows every 2D window contained the identical n=5 points; a 4-parameter fit to the same 5 points trivially reproduces itself, and R2=0.9993 with one degree of freedom is not evidence of robustness.

Finalizes G with the const+Lorentzian fit (offset=9304, gamma=485) and calls the values 'consistent and reproducible' after stating in Step 23 that such an offset is 'clearly unphysical' (local background ~37000) and the model 'ill-posed and window-dependent'. Step 20's sensitivity output showed offset swinging from -40127 to 9304 and gamma from 485 to 780, and the Step 24 'key realization' (x0~19140, gamma~180) is silently dropped, so the run stops despite unresolved evidence.

notes: A correct solution had to establish what the file's x-axis represents (its 1648-47183 range and ~500-fold variation in sampling density show it is not a plain cm^-1 Raman-shift axis), locate the graphene G and 2D features on that basis, and fit each with a Lorentzian plus offset. At Step 10 the agent instead assigned G and 2D to the two tallest features by absolute height (x~19140 and the ~9% hump at x~33245) on a loose ratio argument, while its own Step 9 binned table showed several far more prominent features (near x~3600-3800, 6200-6400 and 10000-10800) it never examined; under the reciprocal transform 1e7/x implied by the sampling pattern, those ignored features fall at ~2703 and ~1587 (the expected 2D and G positions) whereas the fitted features map to ~522 and ~301, the well-known silicon substrate bands. Every subsequent fit therefore targeted the wrong peaks, and the G fit was finalized at Step 26 with a window-dependent offset the agent itself had called unphysical. The misidentification is material because it determines every value written to /app/results.json.
